title: Adjectives and Opposites
sourceNote: The auto-captions for this video are heavily garbled. Some example sentences (for example the ones for 'alt', 'dick/dünn' and 'teuer/billig') could not be reconstructed with certainty, so the examples here use the clearly recognisable word pairs; extra examples are marked as supplementary.
objectives: I can name common adjectives together with their opposites
I can describe people and things with the pattern 'X ist + adjective'
I can use aber to contrast two statements
I can tell the two meanings of alt (old person / old thing)

patterns.ex: Paul ist glücklich, aber Robert ist traurig.
patterns.en: Paul is happy, but Robert is sad.

grammar.title: Learn adjectives in pairs
grammar.body:
The teacher's main tip: always learn an adjective **together with its opposite**. One word reminds you of the other, so both stay in your memory.

The pairs of this lesson: **groß – klein**, **langsam – schnell**, **glücklich – traurig**, **lang – kurz**, **dumm – intelligent**, **gut – schlecht**, **leicht – schwer**, **alt – jung / neu**, **dick – dünn**, **teuer – billig**.
grammar.ar: تعلّم كل صفة مع ضدّها حتى تتذكرهما معًا.

grammar.title: Adjective after sein: no ending
grammar.body: When the adjective stands after **sein** (*ist, sind, bin*), it does not change. It is always the same basic form, whether the subject is a man, a woman or a thing.

examples.de: Paul ist glücklich, aber Robert ist traurig.
examples.en: Paul is happy, but Robert is sad.

examples.de: Der Mann ist dumm, aber der Fuchs ist intelligent.
examples.en: The man is stupid, but the fox is intelligent.

grammar.title: alt: two contexts
grammar.body: Just like English *old*, **alt** is used for people and for things. But the opposite is different: for a person the opposite is **jung** (young), for a thing it is **neu** (new).
grammar.ar: alt للأشخاص ضدها jung، وللأشياء ضدها neu.

examples.de: Der Mann ist alt, aber das Kind ist jung.
examples.en: The man is old, but the child is young.

grammar.title: Contrast with aber
grammar.body: **aber** (but) joins two statements. Put a comma before it. Each part keeps its own verb in second position.

examples.de: Er ist schnell, aber sie ist langsam.
examples.en: He is fast, but she is slow.

mistakes.why: After *ist* the adjective has no ending.
For people the opposite of *alt* is *jung*; *neu* is for things.

pronunciation.tip: Round your lips as for 'oo' but say 'ee'. *glücklich*, *dünn*.
After i, soft 'ch' like a hissing 'h'. *glücklich*, *billig* (ends in a soft 'ch' sound).

lines.de: Nein, er ist langsam. Er ist groß.
lines.en: No, he is slow. He is big.

lines.de: Der Fuchs ist klein, aber er ist schnell und intelligent.
lines.en: The fox is small, but he is fast and intelligent.

tip: Make flashcards with one adjective on the front and its opposite on the back.

comprehension.q: What is the teacher's tip for learning adjectives?
comprehension.a: Always learn them together with their opposites.

comprehension.q: What is the opposite of 'alt' for a person?
What is the opposite of 'alt' for a thing?

exercises.title: Match the words
exercises.instructions: Match each German adjective with its English meaning.

items.q: Der Mann ist alt, aber das Kind ist ___.
items.expl: For people the opposite of *alt* is *jung*.

items.q: I am small, but he is big.
items.a: Ich bin klein, aber er ist groß.

summary: Learn adjectives together with their opposites.
After *sein* the adjective has no ending: *Der Elefant ist langsam.*
Pairs: groß–klein, langsam–schnell, glücklich–traurig, lang–kurz, dumm–intelligent, gut–schlecht, leicht–schwer, dick–dünn, teuer–billig.
alt has two opposites: jung (people) and neu (things).
Use *aber* with a comma to contrast two statements.
